name: Sparse Attention with Linear Units
problem: Sparse attention is usually obtained by sparsifying SOFTMAX, which needs approximations of the softmax function and ties sparsity to the softmax's behaviour.
mechanism: Replace the softmax with a ReLU: Rectified Linear Attention (ReLA). Sparsity emerges NATURALLY from the ReLU formulation - negative scores produce exactly zero output - rather than being imposed by a separate sparsity mechanism. Training stability is obtained with layer normalisation plus either a specialised initialisation or an additional gating function. A property no softmax-sparsified alternative has: heads can learn to attend to NOTHING for some queries, i.e. switch themselves off.
speedup_reported: NOT A QUANTIFIED SPEEDUP. The abstract reports quality parity and structural efficiency: translation performance comparable to strong baselines across five machine translation tasks, with training and decoding speed SIMILAR to vanilla attention, plus high sparsity rate and head diversity and better source-target alignment accuracy than sparsified-softmax models. 'Similar speed to vanilla attention' plus emergent sparsity is the claim - the sparsity rate is a property, not a measured serving win.
notes: arXiv ID 2104.07012 verified via abs-page citation_title/citation_date on 2026-10-03; title matches. Two cautions recorded because the name is a trap: (1) an OpenReview search for this title returns a DIFFERENT paper's records, 'SEA: Sparse Linear Attention with Estimated Attention Mask' (ICLR 2024 poster) - unrelated; (2) this 2021 encoder-decoder machine-translation work is not the ancestor of the linear-attention serving kernels in this repo - those descend from linear-transformers and gated/SSD variants (mamba-2, kimi-linear), which use softmax-derived kernel feature maps, not ReLU.
